_what_this_is: A SHELF, as bin/shelf_index.py writes it, with the labels already filled in so you can see what a finished one looks like. You do not write this file by hand: point shelf_index.py at a folder of clips and it measures everything below the label line. Then you open the frames it extracted, look at them, and fill in label and keywords. bin/broll_reel.py reads this plus a cut list and decides which clip goes over which words.
_the_paths_below_do_not_exist: On purpose, the same as specs/example-broll.json. Run broll_reel.py against this file as it ships and it names every missing clip and writes nothing, which is what it does with a typo in a real shelf. To see the whole thing work, index a real folder: python3 bin/shelf_index.py footage/cruise --out specs/shelf-cruise.json
_what_is_measured_and_what_is_not: duration_s, width, height, rotation, aspect, orientation, fps, codec, has_audio and bytes come off the file with ffprobe. label, keywords, usable, focus_x, focus_y and note do not, and shelf_index.py writes them empty. There is no vision call in the indexer and no guessing from a filename, because a wrong label puts the wrong picture over her words and nothing downstream would catch it.
_keywords_are_the_whole_mechanism: A clip lands on a beat because one of its keywords appears in the words she says over that beat. So keywords are not tags for a library: they are the words a script would actually use when this picture fits. For a shot of open water, "ocean" and "water" are obvious and "quiet", "alone" and "start" are the ones that earn their place, because those are the words a voiceover reaches for. A clip with one keyword gets used once.
_usable: usable false keeps a clip on the shelf and out of every reel: a blurry take, a wobble, somebody walking through frame. It is kept rather than deleted so a re-index does not keep offering it to you.
_focus: focus_x and focus_y choose what a cover crop keeps when the clip is the wrong shape for a 9:16 frame. 0.5 is centre. On a horizontal clip of two people, 0.35 keeps the one on the left. On a horizon, centre is right and the crop costs nothing.
